newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's airline may sue top-selling U.S. author.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's airline may sue top-selling U.S. author.

text.p: Portuguese airline TAP said on Friday that it might sue top-selling U.S. author Michael Crichton over an air safety thriller in which refers to "inept" maintenance at a company he calls 'Air Portugal'.

Crichton, whose successes include Jurassic Park, wrote in 'Airframe', his latest blockbuster about the mysterious, 10,000-metre plunge of a plane, that maintenance at Air Portugal was "so inept" that it almost caused a serious accident.
TAP-Air Portugal is the full name of the state airline.
Company chairman Manuel Ferreira Lima said that TAP had turned the matter over to a leading Portuguese lawyer for an opinion.
"It is either a question of ignorance, because everybody knows that TAP enjoys a high reputation for safety...a moment of absentmindedness...or bad faith," Ferreira Lima told TSF radio.
The company recently reached an accord with Air France under which the two European airlines will exchange maintenance contracts.
